output.title: Spot trial expiry before it becomes a surprise
output.body:
If you run a small business, spotting trial expiry early is less an AI strategy question than a simple workflow decision: when should an alert fire, and who should see it first? The useful diagnostic is whether your trial dates already live in one place—calendar, email, spreadsheet, or CRM—or whether they are scattered across vendor accounts. If they are central, a light reminder rule may be enough. If they are scattered, you are probably looking at a small integration job, not a full overhaul.

Keep the human in charge. Automation should surface the date; the owner still decides whether to renew, downgrade, or cancel. That matters because money movement and other high-risk decisions stay with a person. AI can notice the deadline, but it should not quietly choose the plan. That would be an efficient way to buy the wrong thing.

One practical next step is to list every SaaS trial you are using and note which tool, if any, already tracks the renewal date. That inventory tells you whether you need a simple reminder, a shared task, or a slightly smarter workflow in your own environment. Bareni starts with that one recurring workflow and keeps the decision bounded. Timings are scopes, not promises; the point is to find the smallest useful control, not to build a maze with a calendar in it.
